Title: The Touch

The other choice was Eve of the War from Jeff Wayne's War of the Worlds musical but I'm not submitting an 11 minute song when the other option is The Touch.

Title: Into the West
Album: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
Comment: When you're young you see Frodo and Bilbo and the Elves getting a reward, but as an adult with more life experiences you realise that it's not that they're choosing to leave the mortal world, but they can longer be a part of it. Be it veterans of war, or other trauma, they can't return to the lives they once lead. Peace and escape is beautiful, but having to leave those you love and who love you, and journey "Into the West", is tremendously sad. I haven't personally struggled with suicidal ideation but I lived with someone who did. I did what I could. It's what you do when you love someone. The song hits me hard whenever I hear it.

Title: Tears for a Father
Comment:
A song from the perspective of a child who's father is in a coma after a car accident. 

This is the first song I specifically remember making me cry. The vocals are so emotive, particularly towards the end with the big sigh and then the child putting on a brave face; gets me nearly every time.

It's mostly written well for the perspective it's supposed to be from too, although I will admit, I'm not a big fan of 'the muddy water makes her smile' ...

Title: You Put a Hex on Me
Comment:
After leaving Norwegian black metal legends Emperor in the early 90s, Mortiis went on to spend the rest of the decade dressed as a troll with a full mask and makeup, creating atmospheric medieval-influenced dungeon synth music. (See: "Child Of Curiosity and The Old Man Of Knowledge" from his album before this, 'The Stargate')

He then made ANOTHER career turn in 2001 and released a synthpop goth-rock album that got compared to New Order, Depeche Mode and others. Ever since he's darted around between the synth-goth, industrial metal and a return to the dungeon synth.

He still dresses like a troll to this day.

Title: My Heart Beat Like A Hammer - Take 2
Comment:
I've gone for the lesser known song, hopefully people judge me based on the improvement from where they came from to where they went.

In the 60s before the relocation to California and Christine McVie, (and later Stevie Nicks and Lindsey Buckingham) joined Fleetwood Mac, they were a psycadelic blues band.

I think most people would agree that their shift to soft/pop rock was a good call.

If you're somehow not familiar with their later work, check out Dreams, Landslide and Rhiannon.

Title: nihilist blues (feat. Grimes)
Comment:
Bring Me went, over the course of two albums, from mostly harsh vocal driven metalcore (Sempiternal) to mostly clean sung metalcore with electronic influences (That's The Spirit) to an album that's mostly slightly moody electronica / electropop / pop-rock (amo). 
I wasn't really much of a fan of BMTH until after amo, to be honest, but their subsequent releases are pretty good, as they've become an interesting blend of their earlier metalcore sound with high-production electronic stuff.
Compare this to something like Shadow Moses from Sempiternal.

This is a massive serve from his usual gritty breakbeat sound to soothing  nu-soul kinda vibe. An excellent album to be honest.

Check out Goldie - Temper Temper to hear just how big of a swerve this is!
